subject: SLA compensation request — HelixGen May 2 incident
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixgen.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixgen.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixGen — request for SLA compensation for May 2 outage

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the post-incident update. We experienced a broad inference failure across our integration between 02:08–02:35 UTC on May 2 which impacted our customer-facing flow and caused roughly 21% request failures for that 27-minute window. Our engineering team captured request traces and we attached a brief downtime extract and our internal impact summary.

Per our SLA (section 4.2), HelixGen is requesting an eligibility evaluation for service credits covering that window. Can you confirm next steps for quantifying the compensation and an expected timeline for issuance? Procurement copied here will need an invoice/credit memo reference if approved.

Appreciate the quick turnaround—this hit a paid feature so it has billing impact.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Director of Platform Engineering
HelixGen

Attachments: downtime_log_20260502.csv, helixgen_impact_summary.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixgen.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HelixGen — request for SLA compensation for May 2 outage

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and the traces. I’m very sorry for the disruption. We’re treating this as a priority.

Quick summary of next steps from our side: 1) we’ll validate incident window and affected requests against our platform logs, 2) compute the SLA credit per your agreement (we will reference section 4.2 and the uptime buckets), 3) route the proposed credit to finance for issuance and provide a credit memo and expected posting date.

I’ve started an internal thread and attached the initial extract we pulled from our side for parity. Can you confirm whether the impact you reported was entirely on the production model route (api.redwood.com/v1/generate) or if any private/dedicated endpoints were involved? That helps finalize the calculation.

Target: provide a quantified credit estimate within 7 business days. If anything changes I’ll escalate.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: helixgen_sla_agreement.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: HelixGen — request for SLA compensation for May 2 outage

Ben / Vanessa — forwarding HelixGen’s request. Key facts: reported 02:08–02:35 UTC May 2, ~21% failures per their trace. They are on a hosted contract (per HG-4531) with the standard uptime buckets in section 4.2 of the SLA.

I pulled our side logs and attached a CSV with the per-minute success/failure counts for the api.redwood.com/v1/generate route for that period. Initial read: our metrics show an aggregated error spike aligning to 02:07–02:36 UTC; the region is us-west. I’ve sketched a preliminary calculation in the attached spreadsheet (sla_calc_sheet_HG4531.xlsx) using the contractual formula: credit = monthly committed spend * (downtime seconds / total seconds in billing period) * multiplier per SLA tier.

Questions for you: 1) do we treat HelixGen’s reported failures as overlapping entirely with our measured errors (yes, looks like it but want confirmation)? 2) Any prior credits this billing period we should net against? 3) Who signs off on the proposed credit amount before finance posts the memo?

I recommend we run the formal calc, confirm with HelixGen, then obtain approval from Ben (finance-ops approval) and Vanessa (CS ownership for customer acceptance). Looking to keep this simple and transparent.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: sla_calc_sheet_HG4531.xlsx, downtime_log_20260502.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelixGen — request for SLA compensation for May 2 outage

Thanks Marissa — I reviewed the spreadsheet. Calculation notes: 1) Confirmed no prior credits for HelixGen this billing month, 2) Our measured downtime window and HelixGen’s traces overlap fully, 3) Monthly committed spend on HG-4531 is $48,000. Using the contractual multiplier for their tier (1.5) and the 27-minute window, I get a proposed service credit of $1,944. See formula tab on the sheet.

I authorize routing this as a standard SLA credit. Please include the credit memo to reference HG-4531 and request accounting to apply it to the June invoice run (posting by June 1). Vanessa — please confirm customer acceptance messaging.

Ben Carter
Finance Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixgen.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixgen.com>

Date: Tue, 1 June 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA compensation request — calculation and credit issuance

Hi Samantha / procurement team — following up with the formal calculation and next steps.

Summary: after reconciling our logs with your traces, we confirm the impact window as 2026-05-02T02:08:00Z through 2026-05-02T02:35:00Z. Using the governance in section 4.2 of the SLA and the committed monthly spend for HG-4531, we computed a service credit of $1,944. This matches the draft in the attached spreadsheet.

What we’re doing next:
- Finance will issue a credit memo referencing deal HG-4531 and post it against the June invoice cycle (expected posting date: 2026-06-03).
- You’ll receive a PDF credit memo and an accounting reference ID when posted.
- CS will follow up to confirm you received the credit and to address any downstream reconciliation items.

If you’d like a one-pager explanation for Procurements or Audit, I can share the calculation excerpt and the incident log extract (attached). Let me know if you prefer the memo sooner; otherwise we’ll proceed with the June posting.

Appreciate your patience and again—sorry for the disruption.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
